Jordan—

Appreciate the attachments. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- Commit model: prefer a tiered-commit ladder. Our finance team wants predictable recognition and a way to scale credits back to our channel if usage grows above thresholds.
- Netback: the 18% must be calculated net of marketplace seller fees (i.e., after platform/marketplace cut). We need the workbook to show both gross and net views for audit.
- Billing path: reseller credits must appear as line-item credits on the marketplace invoice so our channel partners see the adjustment directly; downstream credits are harder for our partners to reconcile.

Two asks before we move to legal: 
1) A worked example showing invoice-level line-item crediting across three months with a trigger at 150% usage (can you populate that in passback_workbook?).
2) A brief note on how refunds/chargebacks are handled if a reseller dispute arises (who owns the liability and how are credits reclaimed).

I'll loop Eric (cc'd) from Finance if needed.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear direction. I updated passback_workbook.xlsx with two scenarios: Tiered commit ladder (baseline + mid + surge) and Single-commit + triggered add-on. Key technical notes I added in the workbook: 

- Netback calc: workbook now includes a column for "marketplace fee" (flat 12%) and deducts that before computing the reseller 18% netback. We also show the alternative of gross passback for comparison.
- Invoice line-item flow: for AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace, our recommended approach is to emit a negative line item per SKU against the monthly invoice. For Azure Offer, we include a short mapping — Azure invoices sometimes require a separate credit note; workbook marks that and flags additional reconciliation steps.
- Chargebacks: initial design is to place liability on CloudBridge for customer-originated disputes (since credits are carved from your gross), with a 30-day window where disputes are handled bilaterally; after 30 days repayment routing reverts to Redwood for proven over-crediting. This is negotiable but intended to keep marketplace invoice flows simple.

I attached a quick sample table in the workbook (sheet: "InvoiceSample_3mo") populated with a 3-month run showing the 150% trigger you asked for.

If this matches, Vanessa can finalize the commercial waterfall and produce the doc for legal.

Lena—

Thanks for the clarity. A few commercial clarifications before we lock: 

- Floor pricing: Redwood proposes a list-price floor on the base commit to protect channel economics. The passback workbook includes sensitivity at -10% / -20% off list. We recommend shallow floors for the first 12 months.
- Escrow / reserve: for the tiered ladder we recommend a 5% escrow against total committed value to cover short-term chargebacks; escrow is refundable at true-up. This reduces counterparty risk and is standard for reseller-heavy deals.
- Discount stacking: confirm whether CloudBridge wants discounts to stack (e.g., committed discount + channel promo). If they stack, we will show netback cascading in the workbook; if not, we will cap so reseller netback stays stable.

Next steps: if you confirm the stacking rule and the escrow, we will produce a final commercial appendix for legal and push to DocuSign (link in my draft).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Channels & Marketplace, Redwood Inference
